policies.title: Current EU, Commonwealth and ECOWAS ordinary-passport short-visit exemption
policies.summary: The central Government's current visitor page expressly exempts United Kingdom, full EU, Commonwealth and ECOWAS citizens for holiday or business visits not exceeding 90 days. This later central guidance resolves contrary rows in GID's older nationality table.
conditions: Only holiday or business visits not exceeding 90 days are within this policy.
The cited central guidance describes citizens; this candidate normalizes the ordinary-passport visitor baseline only.
Employment, residence, transit, health, security and admission-screening requirements are outside this baseline.
This current central guidance supersedes only the table rows that directly contradict its named membership categories.

policies.title: ECOWAS transitional visa-free movement for Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger
policies.summary: Although Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger withdrew from ECOWAS, its current official transition statement directs all ECOWAS member-state authorities to continue visa-free movement for their citizens until further notice.
conditions: The ECOWAS instruction is expressly temporary: it applies until further notice.
The Gambia is a current ECOWAS Member State and is within the authorities addressed by the instruction.
This is limited to the ordinary visitor-access baseline; other admission conditions remain outside scope.

policies.title: Named reciprocal ordinary-passport visa exemptions outside membership groups
policies.summary: GID's current nationality table expressly names San Marino, Tunisia and Russia in its visa-exemption-agreement category. Indonesia is excluded because the same table separately calls for entry clearance.
conditions: The policy uses only named states not already covered by the Government's membership-group exemption.
The GID schedule's contradictory Indonesia rows are deliberately held rather than normalized.
Admission, security, health, work, residence and transit requirements are outside scope.

policies.title: Named visa-and-entry-clearance ordinary passports
policies.summary: GID's live nationality schedule expressly assigns these passports to both visa and entry-clearance categories. The current entry guidance requires an approved clearance before travel, so they remain advance-permission access rather than eVisa, ETA or arrival issuance.
conditions: The schedule explicitly says both visa and clearance are required for this cohort.
GID requires a copy of approved entry clearance for travel; its stated validity is 30 days.
The GID service describes visas as stickers or endorsements, not electronic issuance.
Work, residence, transit, health, security and special-document rules remain outside the ordinary visitor baseline.

policies.title: Named entry-clearance-only ordinary passports
policies.summary: GID's live nationality schedule expressly places these passports in clearance-only categories. Its entry guidance makes approval a pre-arrival condition, not an ETA, eVisa, visa-free route or arrival-issued visa.
conditions: The schedule expressly identifies this cohort as requiring entry clearance only.
GID says clearance must be approved before arrival and carried for entry.
The clearance format and application channel are not established as an ETA or eVisa.
Admission, work, residence, transit, health, security and special-document conditions remain outside scope.

policies.title: Named visa-only ordinary passports: visa issued at entry
policies.summary: GID's live nationality schedule calls these passports visa-only, without clearance. Its current entry guidance expressly makes a visa available from immigration officers at gazetted ports, establishing arrival issuance for this named cohort.
conditions: The GID schedule explicitly separates this visa-only cohort from the entry-clearance categories.
GID says a visa can be acquired from immigration officers at gazetted ports of entry.
The service describes sticker or endorsement issuance, not an eVisa.
Admission, work, residence, transit, health, security and special-document requirements remain separate.

conflicts.explanation: The current central Government page expressly exempts Commonwealth citizens; Gabon is a current Commonwealth member. This resolves GID's older contrary visa-and-clearance table row.
GID's current nationality schedule expressly places São Tomé and Príncipe in its clearance-only African cohort, and the entry guidance makes approved clearance pre-arrival.
